structure.heading: Critical Skill Gaps and Talent Acquisition Strategy: Internal Mobility vs. External Hiring
text_content: **Critical Skill Gaps and Talent Acquisition Strategy: Internal Mobility vs. External Hiring**

In 2026, 58% of net new roles (81 of 140) are recommended to be filled via internal mobility to preserve institutional knowledge, reduce onboarding time, and increase retention. The Talent Acquisition and People & Culture teams will prioritize internal pipelines for roles with close adjacency to current skill sets, notably product management, customer success, and sales operations. This internal-first posture enables accelerated ramp-up, lower hiring costs, and clearer career pathways that support organizational continuity during capacity growth.

The most significant external hiring requirement is Data Engineering, with 24 hires planned in 2026 to meet analytics scalability and platform initiatives. External recruiting will be reserved for roles where internal depth is insufficient—advanced data engineering, cloud platform architects, and specialized ML infrsatructure egnineers. Time-bound operational targets include a target time-to-fill of 45 days for priority roles, effective 2026-01-01, with Talent Acquisition deploying expedited sourcing, assessment, and offer protocols to meet this SLA.

Implementation will combine structured internal mobility pathways with targeted external sourcing, supported by learning investments and governance. Key actions include: 1) scaling cross-functional rotations and stretch assignments; 2) funding role-specific upskilling tied to competency passports; 3) instituting monthly hiring and mobility dashboards reporting time-to-fill, acceptance rate, and internal placement. Success metrics will track internal conversion, cost-per-hire, and quarterly reviews led by Pepole & Culture and Talent Acquisition under oversight.

structure.heading: 2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Drivers
text_content: **2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Drivers**

As of 2025-12-31 the organization employs 1,240 FTE, and the workforce plan forecasts a rise to 1,380 FTE by 2026-12-31, an absolute increase of 140 FTE (11.3%). This planned expansion is driven by three primary capacity requirements: accelerated product development, expanded customer success support for enterprise accounts, and strengthened compliance and security functions to meet 2026 regulatory milestones. The timeline for this headcount increase is phased across four quarters in 2026 to align with fiscal budget windows and project delivery gates and resource planning.

Engineering headcount is forecast to increase from 410 FTE to 470 FTE in 2026, a net addition of 60 FTE (14.6%), concentrated in software development, site reliability engineering (SRE), and data engineering roles. This increase addresses capacity drivers including a company-wide cloud migration, two major product launches scheduled for H1 and H3 2026, and an acceleration of AI-enabled feature work. Hiring will emphasize mid-senior level engineers with cloud-native and security competencies, with an anticipated average ramp time of 4–6 months per hire overall.

The remaining workforce expands from 830 FTE (non-engineering) as of 2025-12-31 to 910 FTE by 2026-12-31 — an increase of 80 FTE (9.6%) distributed across sales, customer success, product management, and compliance. Capacity drivers here include scaling account management for larger deals, augmenting regulatory teams for EU and APAC filings, and increasing product management to support roadmap velocity. Operationally, this shift requires updated workforce capacity models, adjusted headcount budgets per quarter, and targeted learning programs to reduce time-to-productivity for hires and internal transfers.
